summary: Correct two high-severity population/endpoint misattributions after targeted primary full-text verification.

old.design_population: Multicenter 2000–2015; 234 attempted resections and 70 entered LT protocols; 191 curative-intent resections and 41 confirmed-CCA LT in recipient analysis.
old.selection: LT patients were younger (52 vs 65), more often PSC(61% vs 2%), and more often treated with chemo/RT(98% vs 57%).
old.results: Recipient 3-/5-year OS 72%/64% LT versus 33%/18% resection. Restricted non-PSC,<3 cm, node-negative comparison favored LT at 5 years 54% vs 29%(p=.03); adjusted/restricted ITT comparison remained significant (p=.049).
old.limits: Conflicting observational evidence versus Dong; major selection/era/therapy confounding. Exact ITT exclusions and time origin require full-PDF recheck; no unsupported ITT rate is reproduced here.
old.locator: Ann Surg 2018; 267: 797–805; primary abstract and indexed Results/Discussion.

new.design_population: Multicenter 2000–2015; 234 attempted resections and 70 entered LT protocols; 191 curative-intent resections and 41 confirmed-CCA LT in recipient analysis.
new.selection: In Table 1, median age was 54 years after LT versus 67 after resection; PSC 61% versus 2%. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy was 95% versus 5%, and radiation 95% versus 3%. These table values differ from the abstract summary.
new.results: Recipient 3-/5-year OS was 72%/64% after LT versus 33%/18% after resection. In the restricted non-PSC comparison against resection for <3 cm, node-negative disease, five-year OS was 54% versus 29% (log-rank P=.03). The restricted intention-to-treat comparison was also significant (log-rank P=.049); this was not a multivariable-adjusted treatment effect.
new.limits: Observational comparison with major selection, PSC, treatment and era differences. Recipient OS starts at surgery. Intention-to-treat OS starts at surgery for attempted resection, but at protocol initiation for LT. Four LT-protocol entrants lacked initiation dates and were excluded from the ITT analysis (66 of 70 analyzed). Restricted analyses do not establish LT superiority for all resectable pCCA.
new.locator: Ethun 2018, Ann Surg267:797–805. Targeted full-text read: p798 Methods/time origins; p799 ITT exclusions and restricted log-rank; p800 Table1. B26/R6 saved primary text29064885.txt.

old.design_population: Observational mixed resection/LT cohort, 52 patients with ctDNA data, 34 preoperative and 18 postoperative tests; only nine paired samples. Abstract-only verification.
old.selection: Guardant360 profiling, variable timing; the 29 mutation types reported are not 29 patients. Not a ctDNA-directed LT eligibility trial.
old.results: All nine paired patients were ctDNA-positive preoperatively; three remained positive postoperatively. Abstract reports postoperative recurrence 57% versus 0% by ctDNA status (P=0.0419).
old.limits: Small numbers, mixed operations, incomplete pairs, possible overlap with other centre cohorts and no strategy comparison. Association supports research and risk discussion, not mandatory negative ctDNA, empirical treatment until negative, or declaring cure from a negative result.
old.locator: JCO Clin Cancer Inform 2023;7:e2300111; PubMed PMID37820293 abstract only.

new.design_population: Observational mixed liver-resection/LT cohort: 52 patients with ctDNA data, 34 assessed preoperatively and 18 postoperatively, with nine sequential pre-/postoperative pairs. The paired cohort includes both operations.
new.selection: Guardant360 profiling, variable timing; the 29 mutation types reported are not 29 patients. Not a ctDNA-directed LT eligibility trial.
new.results: All nine sequentially tested patients were ctDNA-positive before surgery; three remained positive afterward. The reported 57% versus 0% recurrence association (P=.0419) concerns recurrence after liver resection, not a transplant-specific recurrence comparison.
new.limits: Small heterogeneous cohort with variable testing and incomplete pairs; no ctDNA-directed allocation or transplant strategy trial. The Results recurrence denominators (14 positive plus six negative) do not reconcile cleanly with the 18 postoperative patients in the abstract/Table1; this needs clarification. Do not infer a mandatory negative-ctDNA selection rule, benefit from empirical treatment until negative, or cure from a negative test.
new.locator: Wehrle2023 JCO Clin Cancer Inform7:e2300111, PMID37820293. Targeted primary full-text Methods/Results, Table1, Table2, Figure1 and Discussion (PDF pp2–6); original B26/R6/_txt/C_37820293.txt.

edits.old: Primary abstract plus indexed full-text excerpts; PDF, exact ITT analytic exclusions and time-origin detail require final full-PDF check.
edits.new: Targeted primary full-text Methods, Table1 and ITT Results read (Ethun2018 pp798–800); not an assertion that every analysis or supplement was audited.

edits.old: Published primary abstract reviewed; complete PDF not available in searched depots/Downloads
edits.new: Targeted primary full-text Methods, Results, Tables1–2 and Discussion read; resection recurrence attribution corrected. Internal postoperative denominator discrepancy remains unresolved.

          "stance": "Use six months of documented stability as an OPEN default for clinically stable HEHE, with explicit exceptions and continued assessment of whether LT is needed.",

            "Do not delay threatening liver failure, significant progressive symptoms or rapid progression solely to complete six months. Obtain urgent multidisciplinary review of LT versus non-LT treatment; urgency does not itself establish oncologic suitability.",
            "Six months is an expert-guidance-informed local default, not a national requirement or validated cutoff. Continued stability does not mandate LT: reassess resection, symptom burden, function and benefit over continued observation."

          "tests": "Expert EHE pathology; complete liver/systemic staging; symptoms and liver function; interval growth and vascular/node assessment; resection review.",

            "ehe_lai",

DGVS explicitly favors six months of largely stable disease. This expert-guidance counterpoint is more conservative than the earlier four-month local proposal; neither interval has causal comparative validation.",
            "counterevidence": "There is no randomized immediate-versus-delayed LT comparison. Time accrued before referral, urgent liver failure, selection to survive waiting, lead time and different OS clocks can generate apparent benefits of observation.",
            "certainty": "Low certainty for selected post-LT survival; very low certainty that a fixed observation interval improves outcomes. No validated universal 120-day eligibility cliff.           "steps": [
            "exception-route"
          ],
          "context": "Review which NLRB recommendation applies, while separately establishing a clinical indication for transplantation.",
          "stance": "Use the four NLRB routes as OR alternatives, then separately prove a clinical indication for LT.",
          "rules": [
            "Document at least one actual guidance route: (1) adenoma with GSD or Abernethy; OR (2) unresectable β-catenin-mutated adenoma; OR (3) unresectable adenoma with adenomatosis >10 lesions (at least 11); OR (4) unresectable AND unresponsive to nonoperative therapy AND progressive or complicated disease.",
            "Do not require all four routes, and do not impose cirrhosis as a national prerequisite. Conversely, meeting one guidance route does not itself justify surgery.",
            "Require specialist pathology/radiology and an alternatives review before requesting an exception; proven malignant transformation must be evaluated under the appropriate cancer pathway."

This expert-guidance counterpoint is more conservative than the earlier four-month local proposal; neither interval has causal comparative validation.",

          "status": "Allocation and clinical review",
          "steps": [
            "exception-route"
          ],
          "context": "Review which NLRB recommendation applies, while separately establishing a clinical indication for transplantation.",
          "stance": "Use the four NLRB routes as OR alternatives, then separately prove a clinical indication for LT.",
          "rules": [
            "Document at least one actual guidance route: (1) adenoma with GSD or Abernethy; OR (2) unresectable β-catenin-mutated adenoma; OR (3) unresectable adenoma with adenomatosis >10 lesions (at least 11); OR (4) unresectable AND unresponsive to nonoperative therapy AND progressive or complicated disease.",
            "Do not require all four routes, and do not impose cirrhosis as a national prerequisite. Conversely, meeting one guidance route does not itself justify surgery.",
            "Require specialist pathology/radiology and an alternatives review before requesting an exception; proven malignant transformation must be evaluated under the appropriate cancer pathway."
          ],
          "tests": "Subtype/β-catenin result where needed; lesion count and distribution; GSD/shunt status; resectability; prior nonoperative treatment and complication record. Record the exact lesion count and, when available, the CTNNB1 exon/activation phenotype; exactly ten is not >10.",
          "allocation": "NLRB wording concerns exception review and remains nonbinding. Submission, eligibility and approval are distinct.",
          "references": [
            "nlrb",
            "acg_fll2024",
            "easl_benign",
            "hca_nault",
            "hca_ziogas"
          ],
          "evidence": {
            "synthesis": "Allocation-route eligibility and clinical necessity must be recorded separately. Lesion number, size and molecular subtype identify different questions. The NLRB four-route OR structure is more permissive than older clinical LT guidance; clinical risk still needs confirmation and alternatives review.",
            "counterevidence": "Adenomatosis is ≥10 in ACG terminology but >10 in the cited NLRB route: exactly ten lesions cannot be silently rounded into >10. Molecular subtypes are not biologically interchangeable. Selected-registry survival does not quantify the benefit of replacing an otherwise functioning liver.",
            "certainty": "High confidence in the meaning of the current guidance text; low certainty for phenotype-specific LT benefit; moderate biological evidence for subtype heterogeneity, not a validated LT threshold.",
